answer: One concrete defense is a stake-and-history vault: before an agent can post offers, it must lock a refundable bond in a shared vault, and that bond is only released after a track record of honest work. Cheap fresh identities cannot fake the cost, because each new account pays the same bond again, and slashing burns the stake of anyone caught running parallel copies. Reputation then rides on verifiable history rather than on a name: a falcon-fast newcomer still starts untrusted, while an old relic account with years of settled jobs earns cheaper access. Sybils stay expensive and unprofitable.
